title: OpenXR Builtin Marker Tracking fails on first install due to permission race condition
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in v4.7.2.stable.official [ed1daf0bf], v4.7.stable.official [5b4e0cb0f]



### System information

Godot v4.7.2.stable - Windows 11 (build 26200) - Multi-window, 3 monitors - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3080 Ti (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.9186) - AMD Ryzen 5 5600X 6-Core Processor (12 threads) - 31.92 GiB memory - WASAPI (44100 Hz, Stereo/mono) - Meta Quest 3

### Issue description

Description:
The MRP is a small AR Marker Tracking App (QR Codes).

What doesn't work:
When installing the MRP for the first time on the Quest 3, OpenXR fails to create a spatial context due to a permissions race condition. This error appears on the connected Godot Editor as soon as the app starts, before the user has had the chance to accept the required "spatial entities" permission.

```
E 0:00:01:584   create_spatial_context: OpenXR: Failed to create spatial context [XR_ERROR_PERMISSION_INSUFFICIENT]
  <C++ Error>   Method/function failed. Returning: Ref<OpenXRFutureResult>()
  <C++ Source>  modules/openxr/extensions/spatial_entities/openxr_spatial_entity_extension.cpp:409 @ create_spatial_context()
```

Even after the permission is accepted, the built-in marker tracking does not register visible markers during that first session. When starting the app for a second time (or deploying a new build with existing permissions), the built-in marker tracking works as intended and gray spheres appear over the QR Codes.

Expected behavior:
OpenXR should either wait for the user to resolve the permission prompt before attempting to create the spatial context, or it should gracefully recover and begin tracking markers once the permission is granted during the initial session.

### Steps to reproduce

#### Setup MRP
1. Install the OpenXR Vendors Plugin from the Asset Store (5.1.0-stable was used).
2. Install the Android Build Template.

#### Build App
1. Remove all previous installations of the app from the Quest 3 to ensure a clean state.
2. Export the Meta Quest 3 build / deploy it directly to the connected headset.
3. As soon as the app opens, observe the `[XR_ERROR_PERMISSION_INSUFFICIENT]` error in the connected Godot Editor console.
4. Note that marker tracking fails to initialize even after granting permissions on the device.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

Godot 4.7.2-stable
[BuiltInMarkerTrackingMRP.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32166300/BuiltInMarkerTrackingMRP.zip)
